- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.75), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% bias to short-term forecast.
- Model overestimates in late horizon (25–30 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5%.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 3–5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% in next 5–7 days unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize downward momentum; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast 3–5 days ahead.
